variants.title: Run one suggestion request
variants.context: One suggestion request runs two timelines. The client owns the draft and stamps it with a version, the gateway builds a bounded context envelope, a region-local model generates candidates under a hard deadline, deterministic gates decide, and the client renders ghost text only if the response still matches the draft.
variants.prompt: A writer pauses mid sentence and the client decides it is eligible to ask for a suggestion. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Deterministic code checks confidence, freshness, prefix identity, policy, language, and account scope.
The gateway authenticates the account, applies feature consent, and includes only approved context fields.
A region-local model produces a small candidate set under a hard compute and queue deadline.
The client stamps the prefix at the cursor with a monotonically increasing draft version.
The client draws the matching candidate as ghost text, or leaves the editor unchanged.

variants.hint: Which side of the system owns the draft, and therefore goes first and last?
variants.explanation: The client is authoritative at both ends: it versions the prefix before the request and decides whether anything renders after it.

variants.prompt: A response comes back carrying draft version 41 while the editor is now at version 43. Put the events in order.

items.text: The client discards the response and the editor continues unchanged.
The client stamps the prefix as draft version 41 and sends the request.
Candidate generation runs inside its deadline and produces a suggestion for that prefix.
The writer types two more characters, so the client advances the draft version to 43.
The response arrives still carrying version 41 in its request metadata.

variants.hint: Cancellation is an optimization; something else is what preserves correctness.
variants.explanation: Version checking keeps a late response safe to discard even when cancellation arrived too late to save the work.

variants.prompt: The safety policy service becomes unreachable while requests are in flight. Put the events in order.

items.text: No ghost text is drawn, and the writer keeps composing the message normally.
The release gate cannot obtain a required safety and account-scope decision.
The gateway assembles a versioned context envelope for the account and region.
The model returns candidates comfortably inside the deadline.
The client qualifies the request locally against consent, prefix length, and recent request timing.

variants.hint: A gate that cannot decide is not a gate that passes.
variants.explanation: Required safety and privacy decisions fail closed: the system suppresses the suggestion rather than bypassing the gate to protect coverage.

variants.title: Trace the whole deadline
variants.context: The deadline covers the whole interactive path, not just inference: client debounce and correlation, the network round trip, authentication and context preparation, queue or batch wait, prefix encoding and decoding, ranking and policy, then the client freshness check and render. Optimizing decoding alone can leave the product slow.
variants.prompt: Order the stages that spend the end-to-end budget, from the keystroke up to response serialization.

items.text: Network round trip to the selected serving region.
Authentication, consent, language detection, and context preparation.
Prefix encoding and candidate decoding.
Queue or dynamic-batch wait before dispatch.
Ranking, policy checks, and response serialization.
Client debounce, serialization, and request correlation.

variants.hint: The first cost is paid before any packet leaves the machine.
variants.explanation: Model inference is one leg among several, so a budget that only measures decoding hides where the deadline actually goes.

variants.prompt: Order the stages a request passes through after it leaves the client, ending at the pixel.

items.text: Authentication, consent, language detection, and context preparation.
Network round trip to the selected serving region.
The client freshness check and the render of ghost text.
Prefix encoding and candidate decoding.
Ranking, policy checks, and response serialization.
Queue or dynamic-batch wait before dispatch.

variants.hint: The last check happens on the machine that owns the draft.
variants.explanation: The client rechecks freshness and prefix identity after the response returns, so the final leg of the budget belongs to the client.

variants.prompt: A cohort is routed to a distant region and misses the 60 ms target even though decoding got faster. Put the legs it spends in order.

items.text: The client rechecks freshness and finds the deadline already spent.
The request crosses a long network path to the policy-compatible region.
The gateway prepares consent, language, and the context envelope.
The batch wait and the encode plus decode work run on the accelerator.
The client debounces the keystroke and correlates the request.

variants.hint: Which leg grew, and which leg did the optimization touch?
variants.explanation: Network distance and batching can consume the deadline before decoding starts, which is why the complete path is budgeted.

variants.title: Size the demand
variants.context: Demand is estimated from eligible typing events, not raw keystrokes: active sessions times requests per minute, converted to a per-second rate. Concurrency is the request rate multiplied by service time, and regional capacity is judged by what the survivors must absorb when a region is removed.
variants.prompt: A busy period has 9,000,000 active compose sessions. After debounce and eligibility each session averages 3 requests per minute. What is the request rate?
variants.hint: The eligibility rate is per minute, but capacity is planned per second.
variants.explanation: 9,000,000 sessions times 3 requests is 27,000,000 per minute, and dividing by 60 seconds gives 450,000 requests per second.

mistakes.feedback: That is the per-minute total, which overstates the serving rate by a factor of 60.
That divides sessions by 60 but drops the three eligible requests each session makes.

variants.title: Size the demand
variants.context: Demand is estimated from eligible typing events, not raw keystrokes: active sessions times requests per minute, converted to a per-second rate. Concurrency is the request rate multiplied by service time, and regional capacity is judged by what the survivors must absorb when a region is removed.
variants.prompt: The service takes 400,000 requests per second and each request occupies a serving slot for 20 ms. How many requests are in flight at once, before any headroom is added?
variants.hint: Concurrency is the arrival rate multiplied by how long each request stays.
variants.explanation: 400,000 per second times 0.02 seconds is 8,000 concurrent requests, and headroom for skew and retries is added on top.

mistakes.feedback: That multiplies by 20 without converting milliseconds into seconds.
That divides the rate by the service time instead of multiplying by it.

variants.title: Size the demand
variants.context: Demand is estimated from eligible typing events, not raw keystrokes: active sessions times requests per minute, converted to a per-second rate. Concurrency is the request rate multiplied by service time, and regional capacity is judged by what the survivors must absorb when a region is removed.
variants.prompt: Traffic is spread evenly across 5 policy-compatible regions. One region is removed and its traffic is absorbed by the others. What share of global traffic must each surviving region now carry, in percent?
variants.hint: Work out how many regions are left before dividing anything.
variants.explanation: Four regions share all the traffic evenly after the loss, so each carries 25 percent instead of 20 percent.

mistakes.feedback: That is the share before the failure, which understates what each survivor must absorb.
That assumes only three regions remain to share the load.

variants.title: Abstain under pressure
variants.context: The suggestion service is not the editor. Under queue pressure, region loss, model failure, or a policy outage the correct move is graceful abstention: shed work, contain the blast radius, and suppress rather than bypass a required gate. The user must still be able to write and send normally.
variants.prompt: Queue age is climbing and many requests will miss their deadline. What is the correct response?
options: Keep every queued request and let the client discard whatever arrives late.
Widen the batch window so accelerator utilization improves while the queue drains.
Cap queue age, dispatch partial batches, and ask clients to reduce request frequency.
optionFeedback: Doing the work anyway burns capacity on responses the client is already guaranteed to throw away.
A longer batch window spends freshness budget and makes the tail worse exactly when the tail is the problem.
Correct: shed work that cannot meet its deadline and push back on demand before the queue grows without limit.
variants.hint: Work that cannot meet its deadline has no value, so what should happen to it?
variants.explanation: Under queue pressure the service sheds undeliverable work and asks clients to back off, rather than trading freshness for utilization.

variants.title: Abstain under pressure
variants.context: The suggestion service is not the editor. Under queue pressure, region loss, model failure, or a policy outage the correct move is graceful abstention: shed work, contain the blast radius, and suppress rather than bypass a required gate. The user must still be able to write and send normally.
variants.prompt: A serving region is lost, and the only region with spare capacity is outside the cohort's permitted data residency. What should happen?
options: Fail over to the available region and record the residency exception for later review.
Queue the cohort's requests until the compliant region returns to service.
Disable suggestions for that cohort while the editor keeps working normally.
optionFeedback: Residency is a policy boundary, and logging an exception afterwards does not undo the transfer.
Holding requests spends the deadline anyway, so the writer waits and still sees nothing.
Correct: route only to policy-compatible regions, and turn the feature off for the cohort when none can meet the deadline.
variants.hint: Which of the two constraints, residency or coverage, is allowed to bend?
variants.explanation: Suggestions are optional and residency is not, so the cohort loses the feature rather than the guarantee.

variants.title: Abstain under pressure
variants.context: The suggestion service is not the editor. Under queue pressure, region loss, model failure, or a policy outage the correct move is graceful abstention: shed work, contain the blast radius, and suppress rather than bypass a required gate. The user must still be able to write and send normally.
variants.prompt: The primary model fails to load on several replicas during a rollout. What is the correct fallback?
options: Keep retrying the primary model on every request until enough replicas recover.
Serve from a smaller model whose release policy and evaluation contract are already approved.
Serve from the newest available checkpoint, since any suggestion beats no suggestion.
optionFeedback: Retrying each abandoned prefix amplifies the outage instead of containing it.
Correct: a fallback path is only safe when its own policy and evaluation contract were approved in advance.
An unapproved checkpoint has no evaluated safety or quality contract, and no suggestion is an acceptable outcome.
variants.hint: What must already be true about a fallback before an incident starts?
variants.explanation: Fallbacks are pre-approved paths, because an incident is not the moment to grant a model a release policy it never had.

variants.title: Give each gate its question
variants.context: Confidence is not permission to render. Independent gates ask separate questions: does the candidate clear the product threshold, did it arrive in time, does it match the current draft, does policy allow it, is it in the language at the cursor, and is it more than a malformed echo of the prefix.
variants.prompt: Match each release gate to the question it answers.

pairs.label: Confidence
pairs.detail: Does the candidate clear the product threshold for this language and length?

pairs.label: Freshness
pairs.detail: Did the response arrive inside the client-visible deadline?

pairs.label: Prefix identity
pairs.detail: Does the response match the current draft version and cursor state?

pairs.label: Safety
pairs.detail: Does deterministic policy allow this content and context class?

pairs.label: Repetition
pairs.detail: Does the text avoid duplicated spans, broken spacing, or a trivial echo of the prefix?

variants.hint: Two of these look like timing; one is about the clock and one about the text.
variants.explanation: The gates are independent, so a candidate renders only when every required one passes.

variants.prompt: Four candidates are suppressed. Match each suppression to the gate that caught it.

pairs.label: Confidence
pairs.detail: A plausible continuation scored below the threshold set for short French prefixes.

pairs.label: Freshness
pairs.detail: A strong candidate arrived 20 ms after the client deadline had already passed.

pairs.label: Prefix identity
pairs.detail: The writer deleted a word, so the returned text no longer continues the draft on screen.

pairs.label: Language
pairs.detail: The prefix is in Portuguese and the continuation came back in English.

variants.hint: One of these candidates was good; it was simply too late.
variants.explanation: Recording the first suppression reason per request is what makes coverage losses diagnosable in aggregate.

variants.prompt: Match each gate to the user-visible failure that appears if it is removed.

pairs.label: Confidence
pairs.detail: Writers are interrupted by weak guesses that cost attention even when ignored.

pairs.label: Freshness
pairs.detail: Ghost text appears after the writer has already moved on.

pairs.label: Prefix identity
pairs.detail: A suggestion attaches to text that is no longer in the draft.

pairs.label: Safety
pairs.detail: Content the policy forbids reaches the editor because a score looked high enough.

variants.hint: Ask what the writer would actually see on screen.
variants.explanation: Each gate exists because of a distinct product failure, which is why one aggregate confidence score cannot stand in for all of them.
